# Video Prompt Router

Turn a Chinese or English video request into a shortlist of prompt templates with explicit evidence and constraints. The router checks duration, shot structure, reference material, dialogue and music requirements. When information is missing, it asks up to three questions that change the shortlist. A host agent then selects a template and writes the prompt.

This repository extends [LearnPrompt/awesome-seedance](https://github.com/LearnPrompt/awesome-seedance). The `feat/video-prompt-router` branch is maintained independently and will not merge into `main`. The added router CI workflow has been removed; validation, builds and installation run locally. Builds use a local data snapshot, do not fetch remote data, and make no daily-sync promise.

The snapshot contains **{{templates}} templates and {{cases}} source cases**: {{filed}} assigned, {{skipped}} deliberately skipped, and {{todo}} awaiting classification. The router selects templates and exposes constraints. Writing a final prompt requires a host agent; generating video requires a separate platform call.

## Desktop theme search

The Windows desktop app searches every template and case using your configured OpenAI-compatible model. Browse videos and original prompts, copy exact text, and inspect Agent relevance judgments after preliminary local results. See [desktop instructions](./DESKTOP-USAGE.md).

```powershell
npm ci
npm run desktop:start
```


## Quick start

The locally validated environment is Node.js 22 and Python 3.10. Routing needs only Node.js; the full build check also needs Python. No npm dependencies or model API keys are required.

```bash
git clone --branch feat/video-prompt-router --single-branch https://github.com/Ryderey/awesome-seedance.git
cd awesome-seedance
node router/route.mjs "15-second multi-shot food ASMR, cooking with melting cheese and steam, no dialogue" --json
```

The output includes `status`, `facets`, `shortlist`, `questions`, `blockedExamples` and `dataVersion`. Check the status and constraints before using a template.

| Status | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| `ready` | Read candidate uses and conditions, select a template, and let the host write the prompt |
| `needs_clarification` | Answer questions, resolve conflicts or confirm pending requirements, then rerun the complete request |
| `no_match` | Inspect hard constraints and model limits; explicitly revise the request or add a template |

## Structured requests and follow-up answers

Save this as `request.json` and run `node router/route.mjs --request request.json --json`:

```json
{
  "text": "Perfume product reference image, 5-second live-action single take, no dialogue, music or captions",
  "top": 5,
  "strictness": "strict",
  "referencePurpose": "product",
  "singleGeneration": true,
  "allowEditing": false,
  "facets": {
    "subjects": ["product"],
    "durationSec": 5,
    "styleMode": "live",
    "shotPlan": "single",
    "hasReference": true,
    "hasDialogue": false,
    "hasMusicSync": false,
    "textOnScreen": false
  }
}
```

Omitted facet fields may be inferred from text; explicit `null` keeps a field unknown, while `false` means an explicit exclusion. `subjects` is an array, and `durationSec` is total video duration. Reference purposes are `identity`, `product`, `first_frame` and `storyboard`; a reference image does not automatically imply a storyboard grid.

Optional `model` selects an adapter. `singleGeneration: true` requires one generation; `allowEditing: false` forbids stitching, trimming and post-production remedies. Preserve the original text, model and other constraints when merging answers into a complete request, then rerun. The CLI is stateless; the host manages the conversation.

## How routing works

1. Extract shooting conditions, distinguishing requirements, negation and unknowns, and record conflicting statements.
2. Apply template hard constraints, then rank by soft alignment and text evidence. Subject words such as “cat” or “car” are not the sole selection criteria.
3. Simulate answers for unknown conditions and ask only questions that change the shortlist, at most three per round.
4. Return intended uses, matching evidence, hard checks, soft differences and pending requirements for the host agent's final selection.

The default shortlist has five candidates and can expand to eight for ties at the cutoff. `ready` means routing conditions are satisfied; it guarantees neither the best first-ranked template nor successful video generation. Compatible candidates without positive evidence still require clarification. See [ROUTER-USAGE.md](./ROUTER-USAGE.md) for the calling contract and [DESIGN-video-prompt-router.md](./DESIGN-video-prompt-router.md) for design notes; both documents are in Chinese.

## Model adapters and execution scope

Templates describe shooting structure; `adapters/` describes model differences. Official documentation was checked on 2026-10-03 for these specific versions and entry points:

| Adapter | Verified documentation scope |
| --- | --- |
| [Seedance](./adapters/jimeng-seedance.json) | Seedance 2.5 `doubao-seedance-2-5-260628`, Volcengine Ark |
| [Kling](./adapters/kling.json) | Kling 3.0 `kling-v3`, official API |
| [Veo](./adapters/veo.json) | Veo 3.1, Gemini API preview |

Capabilities use `true`, `false` and `null` for documented support, lack of support and unknown status. Unsupported hard requirements always exclude a candidate. For unverified hard requirements, `strict` excludes the candidate and `lenient` retains it pending confirmation. Soft capabilities expose adapter fallback actions or unresolved requirements. Duration changes, shot splitting, audio substitution and editing must respect the request and receive user confirmation. Requirements must never be silently rewritten.

Historical “即梦 / Dreamina” aliases currently resolve to the Ark scope; `flow` resolves to the Gemini API scope. These aliases do not verify the corresponding web clients. Adapter files retain official source evidence. No paid video API execution has been tested by this project; documentation checks are not execution results.

## Local validation, packaging and installation

```bash
# Rebuild and validate a temporary snapshot without changing source or installation
node router/build.mjs --check

# After successful validation, update generated files and create a standalone Skill package
node router/build.mjs --write --out .tmp/router-package
```

Checks cover routing behavior, fixed summaries, user requests, JS/Python tests, internal links and standalone package execution. Set `ROUTER_PYTHON` to a Python executable if automatic detection fails.

Replace `YOUR_SKILL_DIRECTORY` with the **video-prompt-router Skill directory** actually read by your host:

```bash
node router/build.mjs --status --target "YOUR_SKILL_DIRECTORY"
node router/build.mjs --install .tmp/router-package --target "YOUR_SKILL_DIRECTORY"
```

Installation validates the manifest and file hashes, stages the package beside the target, switches directories and verifies the result. Failures restore the previous package; the latest complete backup is `<target>.backup`. Unknown files are preserved, while edits to managed files stop an update. Explicitly add `--migrate-legacy` only when taking over an older same-name Skill without a manifest. Restart or reload the host to use the Skill; the host handles questions, selection and prompt writing.

## Completed work and remaining tasks

Implemented: intent extraction, three-state conditions, shared hard and soft scoring, meaningful questions, full-request reruns, capability gates, fallback confirmation, snapshot builds, hash checks and installation rollback. All 53 previously unassigned cases were reviewed: 47 received template labels and six retain justified `null` assignments, leaving no classification backlog. See the [case review](./REVIEW-case-taxonomy-2026-10-03.md).

Remaining work:

- Independent human blind evaluation on new inputs, and independent review of the case classifications.
- More multi-turn regression cases; the post-answer retention check currently covers only {{after_count}} case.
- Host testing from request and final template selection through prompt writing and finished video.
- Verification of unknown capabilities, specific client entry points and real API execution.
- Real Windows file-lock scenarios; current rollback and lock checks include injected failures.

CI is no longer part of the router optimization tasks for this branch. The [optimization plan](./PLAN-video-prompt-router-optimization-2026-10-03.md) and [review record](./REVIEW-video-prompt-router-2026-10-03.md) track detailed progress in Chinese.

## Evaluation and limitations

Results come from [data/router-stats.json](./data/router-stats.json), measured on {{measured_at}}. Top-5 retention measures whether acceptable templates remain among the first five candidates, averaged across labels. It is not final-selection accuracy or video-generation success.

| Measurement | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Frozen-summary Top-5 retention ({{fixed_rows}} rows) | {{fixed_top5}} |
| Current-summary Top-5 retention ({{current_rows}} rows) | {{current_top5}} |
| Sufficient-user-input Top-5 retention ({{sufficient_rows}} / {{user_rows}} rows) | {{user_top5}} |
| Average returned candidates on the frozen set | {{avg_candidates}} |
| Average eligible templates before truncation / {{templates}} | {{avg_eligible}} |
| Question trigger rate on the frozen set | {{asked_rate}} |

Frozen summaries share a source with title-derived terms, and user cases are project-authored; neither replaces independent blind evaluation. The synthetic-facet oracle shares production scoring and is not a generalization ceiling. Every frozen input still triggers questions, so a reduced questioning burden has not been demonstrated. Thresholds are in [eval/thresholds.json](./eval/thresholds.json); the statistics file above contains the detailed `report`. Reproduce results with `node eval/score.mjs --json` using the [evaluation runner](./eval/score.mjs).

## Editing and maintenance

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `router/` | Routing code, facet profiles, capability mappings and lexicon |
| `adapters/` | Model versions, entry points, capability evidence and fallbacks |
| `data/` | Upstream case snapshot, local templates, taxonomy and generated index |
| `eval/` | Frozen baselines, user cases, thresholds and reports |
| `scripts/readme/` | Source copy for the three README languages |
| `scripts/`, `docs/`, `agents/` | Generators, template and gallery documents, Skill artifacts |

After editing sources, run `--write`, then `--check`, and commit sources with their generated outputs to this branch. README counts and measurements are filled by the generator; edit `scripts/readme/` rather than generated README files. New templates need profiles, capability tags, lexicon and taxonomy references, plus at least four Chinese/English user cases, two with sufficient shooting detail. Deleting or renaming a template requires migrating old references.
